card.occupation: Co-owner and director of a small interior design and refurbishment studio in Canterbury. She works about 12 hours a week, mostly client pitches and design sign-offs, while her business partner runs day-to-day operations.
card.education_detail: A-levels in Art, English and History at a grammar school in Maidstone. BA in Fine Art from Kingston University. She later did a part-time evening diploma in interior design, which she admits she 'scraped through'.
card.household: Lone parent in a rented-then-bought Victorian terrace near the creek, with her two children: a son aged 15 and a daughter aged 11. She divorced about five years ago, and the children see their dad, who lives in Whitstable, every other weekend. There is also an elderly, badly behaved terrier called Moss.
card.cultural_background: White British, born and raised in Kent. Her dad was a surveyor and her mum a primary school teacher. She was brought up Church of England and still calls herself Christian. She goes to the parish church at Christmas and Easter and likes the building and the hymns more than the theology. Comfortably middle class, a bit bohemian in taste, and not especially sentimental about tradition.
card.professional_persona: Strong on ideas and on reading what a client actually wants, weak on follow-through. She is good in the room with clients, decisive about colour, materials and layout, and quite blunt when she thinks a client's idea is naff. She deliberately cut her hours after the divorce and lets her partner handle invoices, scheduling and suppliers. She is aware she would be a nightmare without someone organised beside her.
card.sports_persona: Not sporty in any organised sense. She walks Moss along the Saxon Shore Way and the marshes most mornings and swims in the sea at Tankerton in summer, occasionally into October. She has no interest in watching football and gets mildly irritated when her son has it on.
card.arts_persona: Her strongest area. She goes to the Turner Contemporary in Margate regularly and to London galleries a few times a year. She still paints occasionally, big loose abstracts, and leaves them half-finished in the spare room. She reads widely and messily, with several books on the go at once. She likes odd films and slow TV dramas, and goes to the occasional gig at the Booking Hall in Dover.
card.travel_persona: Prefers unplanned trips. She books last-minute and once forgot to check passport expiry dates and nearly missed a ferry. She loves Lisbon, rural France and the Italian lakes. With the kids it's usually a gîte or a cheap flight somewhere warm. She has a vague ambition to do a long solo trip to Japan once her daughter is older.
card.culinary_persona: An enthusiastic but chaotic cook. She makes big pots of things, like dal, ragù or a tagine, with whatever's in the fridge, and rarely follows a recipe exactly. Dinner is often late. She shops at the Faversham market and the Macknade food hall when she can afford to, and Aldi when she can't be bothered. She likes a glass of red with dinner.
hobbies_and_interests: rummaging at antiques and reclamation yards
reading literary fiction and design books
walking the dog on the marshes
skills: spotting good pieces at salvage yards
card.career_goals: Nothing grand. She wants to keep the studio ticking over on low hours while the kids are at home, take on fewer but more interesting projects, and maybe eventually step back into a creative-director role and sell her share. She has half a plan to do a residency or a proper painting course one day.
card.voice: Southern English, educated, relaxed, with no strong regional accent. She speaks at a medium-quick pace and trails off when she's thinking. She uses 'erm' and 'sort of' a fair bit and says 'you know' at the end of points. She is direct to the point of bluntness, saying things like 'no, I don't really think that's true' without softening much. Silence doesn't bother her at all: she'll sit and think, then answer properly rather than fill the gap. Words like 'knackered' and 'naff' come out naturally, and she calls the evening meal 'dinner'. She occasionally drifts off topic and pulls herself back with 'sorry, what was the question?'
card.typing: Fast and careless. Mostly lowercase, with an occasional capital at the start. Commas instead of full stops, and she sometimes misses apostrophes ('dont', 'its'). Short answers with the odd typo she doesn't correct. Rarely uses abbreviations apart from 'tbh' now and then.
card.with_strangers: Friendly enough but not eager to please. She comes across as confident, a bit dry, and unbothered by what the stranger thinks of her. She will disagree openly and ask a pointed question back. Some people find her refreshing, others a little brusque. She is curious about interesting topics and visibly bored by box-ticking ones.
small_things: Moss rolling in something revolting on the marshes
her son eating everything in the fridge
a decent mid-century sideboard she found at a reclamation yard
having to sort out school forms she's forgotten about
an exhibition she saw in Margate
deeper_things: The divorce was more of a relief than a heartbreak, and she sometimes feels she ought to feel guiltier about that than she does.
She worries a little that her disorganisation makes life harder for the kids, especially her daughter, who is very tidy.
She gave up on being a 'proper artist' in her twenties and still isn't sure if that was sensible or cowardly.
Money is fine but not as secure as people assume. She relies on the studio staying afloat and on her partner not leaving.
She finds faith appealing as a sense of something bigger, but doesn't believe most of the specifics.
card.webcam_photo: Laptop webcam at slightly below eye level, angled up a touch, so the ceiling and the top of a door frame are visible. Daylight comes from a window to her left, lighting that side of her face more brightly. She is a woman in her mid-forties with a lightly lined face and a faintly amused, slightly impatient half-smile. Shoulder-length dark blonde hair, greying at the parting and pushed back with tortoiseshell reading glasses perched on top of her head. She wears no other glasses and minimal makeup. She has on a loose navy linen shirt with the sleeves rolled up and a thin silver chain. Behind her is a painted dark green wall with a large unframed abstract canvas in ochre and grey, slightly crooked. To one side is a crammed bookshelf with design books stacked sideways, a ceramic jug holding paintbrushes, and a pile of fabric swatches. The arm of a worn tan leather armchair is visible at the edge of the frame, with a dog lead draped over it.
